jobs.occupation: Maternity Cover - Associate Category Manager, Indirect Spend
jobs.description:
Are you a proactive and results-driven professional eager to make a significant impact in the green energy sector? Semco Maritime is offering a unique, temporary opportunity for an Associate Category Manager to join our team for a minimum of 12 months maternity cover.

**Your position

**As an Associate Category Manager for Indirect Spend you will play a pivotal role in leading category strategies across various sectors including facility management, professional services, travel, and more. This role is perfect for someone who thrives in negotiating and driving cost efficiencies while promoting sustainable practices within the supply chain.

At Semco Maritime safety is a core value, and in this role, you will contribute to maintaining and promoting a strong safety culture while delivering innovative solutions. Above all, your work will make a real change for the global energy sector.

Your workplace will be located at our Global Headquarters in Esbjerg, positioned at the heart of the Danish energy industry with stunning waterfront views. This is a full-time, temporary maternity cover for a minimum duration of 12 months.

**Your Tasks & Responsibilities

**As an Associate Category Manager, your primary responsibility will be to support our Group Support Functions, including HR, Marketing and IT, with strategic procurement and day-to-day purchasing activities. You will also manage indirect spend, with particular responsibility for facility management, including Travel.

• Group Support Functions: Partner with functions such as HR, Marketing and IT to understand their requirements and provide procurement support aligned with business needs.

• Contract Negotiation: Lead and support supplier negotiations to achieve competitive pricing and favourable terms and conditions.

• Purchase Order Management: Coordinate and issue purchase orders, follow up on invoice handling and help ensure compliance with the procurement-to-pay process.

• Cost Management: Maintain visibility of expenditure, support budget control and identify opportunities to reduce costs and improve commercial value.

• Indirect Spend and Facility Management: Manage relevant indirect spend categories, including facility management services, and support effective supplier performance and service delivery.

• Group Travel: Manage the travel category across the Semco Group, including supplier relationships, commercial agreements, cost optimisation and stakeholder support.

**Your Profile & Qualifications

**We are looking for an outgoing and positive individual who is passionate about indirect spend and wants to leave their personal mark on it. You have a proactive and organised approach to your work and are eager to enhance your skills within the department.

• Minimum experience of 2 years in Strategic Procurement or a related commercial field, experience in indirect spend is advantageous but not required.

• Excellent negotiation and relationship-building skills, capable of interacting effectively across diverse cultures and functions. Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize effectively.

• Positive, proactive, and a team player with the autonomy to operate independently.

• Fluent in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

**Welcome to Semco Maritime

**At Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the global energy sector. With us, you will join a community of over 2,300 of the most dedicated thinkers and doers in the energy industry who are driving real change and making their own personal mark on the global energy landscape.

While everyone knows why the energy transition is vital, we are concerned with the journey. How to get there. By providing the answers needed to make change real. Because we believe that global energy ambitions can only be realized through hard work and clever, pragmatic solutions. This is what we do. This is what we invite you to participate in.

Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a sustainable energy future.

So yes, working for us will change the energy sector – and may well change you too.

We know that our people are our greatest strength. We strive to build an inclusive workplace where everyone can be themselves, contribute their perspectives, and feel part of the team. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and believe that diverse teams help us find better solutions and move the energy transition forward.

Care to join the movement?

Change. With us.

At ABB, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

**This position reports to:

**Project Operations Manager

__

**Your role and tasks

**We are looking for a Project Manager to lead service, upgrade, retrofit and modification projects within automation and control systems delivered to energy sector process- or offshore industry. In this role, you will take ownership of your own projects and play a key part in ensuring successful delivery for customers within either the energy sector, process- & production industry or to offshore clients (e.g. power plants, district heating facilities, waste incineration plants).

Working closely with customers, engineering teams and experienced project management colleagues, you will be involved throughout the entire project lifecycle, from planning and coordination to execution and completion. This position offers an excellent opportunity to further develop your project management career while gaining exposure to technically advanced solutions, customer collaboration and commercial project execution in an international organization. If you enjoy taking ownership, building relationships and turning plans into successful project deliveries, this could be the ideal next step in your career.

**Your Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Managing service, retrofit and upgrade projects from tender phase through execution and final delivery.

• Leading project planning, scheduling, resource plans and execution activities.

• Building strong customer relationships and acting as a trusted advisor throughout the project lifecycle.

• Managing commercial risks, project changes, claims and recovery actions.

• Project financials steering, including forecasting, cost control and value optimization.

• Identifying & pursuing aftermarket opportunities for upselling.

• Driving contract management and change management activities.

• Ensuring compliance with ABB quality, cybersecurity and HSE requirements.

**Qualifications For The Role

**

• 4–7 years of project management experience within technical, industrial or automation-related environments.

• Proven experience managing project financials, commercial risks and contractual obligations.

• Solid experience leading project teams and driving delivery towards agreed goals and milestones, including experience with remote management.

• Experience working with customers and cross-functional stakeholders in complex project environments.

• Strong understanding of project planning, budgeting and project execution methodologies.

• Experience delivering projects from tender phase through commissioning and handover.

• Knowledge of automation, OT or industrial control systems, preferably within energy, process, power or offshore industries.

• Excellent communication skills in English and experience working with tools such as Azure DevOps, Microsoft Project or similar. PMP, PRINCE2, IPMA or a comparable project management certification is considered an advantage.

**More About Us

**At ABB, we have a clear goal of promoting diversity and inclusion in terms of gender, LGBTQ+, disability, ethnicity, and age. Together, we have embarked on a journey where we all individually and collectively celebrate and welcome individual differences. You can look forward to joining an organization that emphasizes employee well-being. Collaboration and team spirit are key words for us and a crucial foundation for reaching our shared goals. We prioritize a good working environment highly and continuously invest in the education and development of you and your colleagues. If you want to read more about our continuous work with the working environment and sustainability, you can find more information at: https://global.abb/group/en/sustainability

You will be based at one of our offices in Ballerup, Middelfart or Esbjerg, alongside your closest colleagues. In addition, we offer the possibility of working from home a few days a week. Since you support customers across Denmark, you can expect some time on the road, as well as occasional international travel - primarily to the other Nordic countries.

The position reports to Head of Project Management in Service, Nicolai Heilskov.

Apply for the job online via our simple and easily accessible system, where you can also sign up to receive notifications on other opportunities within ABB. If you have questions about the position before then, you are welcome to contact Nicolai Heilskov at +45 21 15 34 38.

The application deadline is 08.11.2026. We look forward to receiving your application.

Does it excite you to work with cell-based assays to advance innovative peptide-based medicines, and do you have experience with assay automation and liquid handlers? If this sounds like you, and you are ready to take on a broad area of responsibilities, then you could be our new colleague.

**Your new position

**As Senior Laboratory Technician, you will be running cell-based assays to screen and profile candidate drugs in collaboration with other technicians and scientists in the Molecular Pharmacology department. In addition, you will also contribute to the optimization and automation of our laboratory workflows. This role offers a unique opportunity to make a significant contribution to the advancement of our projects by delivering high-quality in vitro data.

**We Offer Exciting Responsibilities

**

• Conducting weekly in vitro assays to assess the efficacy of new peptide drug candidates

• Contributing to the development and improvement of laboratory workflows, with a focus on automation of cell-based assays

• Planning and execution of practical laboratory work

• Processing instrument data in specialized software and databases

• Documentation of laboratory work in the electronic laboratory notebook system

• Responsibilities for maintenance of the lab and lab equipment

• Good collaboration both within and across departments to ensure pace, quality, and exchange of experimental methods and ideas

**Your profile

**You have a mindset aligned with the Zealand values, with curiosity to acquire new skills and learn new methods. You bring a positive attitude and drive, and work both independently and collaboratively. You communicate clearly and have a good understanding of written and spoken English (company language).

**Further, You Have

**

• Education as laboratory technologist, laboratory technician, medical laboratory scientist or similar with at least 3 years of experience with laboratory work

• Proficiency in cell-based assays, including intracellular signaling assays

• Experience with assay automation, including setup and use of liquid handlers

• Hands-on experience with cultivation of mammalian cells

• Strong documentation skills and proficiency with data analysis in Excel, GraphPad Prism or similar software

**Your new team

**You will be part of a department of 17 scientists and 9 technicians dedicated to advancing research and development through generation of in vitro pharmacology and biomarker data, and development of cell-based model systems to deepen understanding of drug mechanism of action. The department is organized into two teams to ensure close managerial support and scientific guidance, and works collaboratively across molecular biology, biochemical, biophysical, and cellular assay platforms to support identification, optimization, and characterization of drug candidates. The position is within our In vitro profiling and signaling team, which focuses on cell-based signaling and binding assays for compound profiling and mechanism-of-action studies.

**Let's bond and be bold

**We have a unique culture, characterized by excellent teamwork and strong engagement across the organization. And we want you to help us strengthen this culture.

Making bonds is at the core of everything we do. From discovering and developing the best new peptide drugs for patients, to engaging with our partners or connecting with each other. We bond through curiosity and playfulness as a team, allowing ourselves to challenge common thinking and drive future innovation. Join us and let's bond and be bold.

Interested in bonding with us? Then please apply no later than November 2nd, 2026, or as soon as possible. The applications will be reviewed as they come in. While a cover letter is not required, please include a few sentences in your CV explaining your motivation for applying.

For further information, please contact Head of In vitro profiling and signaling, Karin Hägerbrand and KHagerbrand@zealandpharma.com.

We are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and welcome applications from all job applicants.

**About Zealand Pharma A/S

**Zealand Pharma A/S (Nasdaq: ZEAL) is a biotechnology company focused on the discovery and development of peptide-based medicines. More than 10 drug candidates invented by Zealand Pharma have advanced into clinical development, of which two have reached the market and three candidates are in late-stage development. The company has development partnerships with a number of pharma companies as well as commercial partnerships for its marketed products. Zealand Pharma was founded in 1998 and is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with a team in the U.S. For more information about Zealand Pharma's business and activities, please visit www.zealandpharma.com.

Finance & Operations Manager

Full-time | On-site in Søborg/Copenhagen | Visibuilt

Join Visibuilt as we take a fossil-free, fermentation-based binder from the lab to the market. We are looking for an experienced financial controller who would like to be the person keeping a growing climate-tech company financially sound, investor-ready and well organised – from the month-end close to the board pack.

Location: Søborg, Greater Copenhagen (on-site)

Start: 1 January 2027 (or as soon as possible)

Type: Full-time employment

Salary: Competitive and in line with the market, reflecting your experience and responsibilities

Reports to: CEO & Founder, Line Kloster Pedersen

Core focus: Financial control and reporting, operations, grants, board and shareholder administration, financial modelling and fundraising support

About Visibuilt

Visibuilt is building fossil-free alternatives for pavement materials. Our core technology, visiBINDER, is a 100% bio-based binder developed from mycelium and designed to reduce energy use and CO2 emissions in infrastructure materials. We are based at Alfa Laval Innovation House in Søborg, just outside Copenhagen.

The role

Visibuilt has grown from an early-stage startup into a company with institutional investors, an active board, several public grant projects and an R&D team whose decisions need solid numbers behind them. You will be our finance and administration function: the person who makes sure our numbers are accurate, on time and useful for decisions – and who owns the operational backbone of the company.

·       A broad role with real ownership. You will be our only finance person, so you plan and manage your own areas – including the operational processes that keep a growing team running – in close collaboration with the CEO, our CTO, our external accountant and payroll administration, auditors and lawyers.

·       Cash is king.  You will own the cashflow budget and rolling forecast, so we always know our runway and spot pinch points well before they arrive. With several grant projects running, customer project, and heavy R&D, this means keeping a close eye on when money actually lands compared with when we spend it.

·       You oversee the bookkeeping. Our external accountant handles the day-to-day entries. Your job is to monitor, quality-check and follow up on their work, and to turn it into reporting the CEO and board can rely on.

·       Real business impact. You get to understand our business and provide market analyses for business development and cost models for R&D.

Responsibilities

Financial control

·       Monitor and quality-check invoicing, payroll and bookkeeping carried out by our external accountant (e-conomic) and approve payments together with management.

Reporting, audit & annual accounts

·       Deliver monthly finance reporting, budget-vs-actual and runway forecasts for management and the board.

·       Take responsibility for the annual accounts and the audit process with our auditors, meeting investor deadlines.

Operations ownership

·       Look after our people operations: keep the employee handbook and policies up to date, and run holiday planning and time registration.

Grant management

·       Manage our public grant portfolio (e.g. EUDP): project budgets, timesheets, reimbursement claims and progress reporting.

·       Support new grant applications with budgets and co-financing plans.

Board, shareholders & governance

·       Act as board secretary: prepare board packs, take minutes and follow up on decisions.

·       Manage shareholder matters – shareholder register, warrant programmes, general meetings, investor reporting and filings with the Danish Business Authority – with support from our lawyers. You coordinate and execute a quarterly shareholder report with the CEO.

Support for business development and R&D

·       Build market analyses (market sizing, segments, pricing) that support the CEO’s commercial work.

·       Build cost models together with R&D and production, so technical choices are informed by unit economics.

Fundraising

·       Be responsible for the financial projections and scenario models used in fundraising and investor dialogues.

·       Maintain our data room and coordinate due diligence processes.

What we are looking for

·       Solid experience in finance – typically 8 years or more – including time as financial controller, finance manager or similar. Experience from audit also counts.

·       Experience with the full finance cycle: month-end close, management reporting, annual accounts and working with auditors.

·       Experience reviewing the work of an external accounting partner.

·       Strong Excel skills: you are comfortable building budgets, forecasts and cost models from scratch.

·       You can explain financial analysis clearly to non-finance colleagues, and you are open about your assumptions.

·       Professional English is required; Danish is strongly preferred.

Nice to have

·       Experience from a start-up, scale-up or SME where you covered a broad range of tasks.

·       Experience managing and reporting on public grants (e.g. Innovation Fund Denmark, EUDP, MUDP or Horizon Europe), including timesheets and reimbursement claims.

·       Fundraising experience: data rooms, due diligence and investor financial models.

·       Board secretary work, shareholder registers, general meetings and company filings.

·       Background from manufacturing, materials or construction – helpful for unit-cost models.

·       Comfortable using AI and automation to speed up routine finance work.

How you work

·       Reliable. You are on time and prepared – especially with investors, auditors and other external partners.

·       You follow through. You see tasks through to completion, and ask for input along the way when you need it.

·       You share your view openly. You raise questions and concerns in the room, and once a decision is made you support it fully.

·       You work in shared systems. Everything lives in the company’s systems and shared drive and you have an eye for making systems more efficient to save time.

·       You use AI with care. For speed – never as a replacement for analysis you have checked yourself.

What success looks like

·       Monthly reporting is delivered on time and of high quality.

·       The annual accounts and audit are completed on time and without surprises.

·       Grant reimbursements and reports are submitted on time, with no rework.

·       Our financial and cost models are up to date and actively used in R&D, business development and fundraising decisions.

·       The data room is kept due-diligence ready, and our operational processes simply work.

What you can expect from Visibuilt

Visibuilt offers the chance to shape the finance and operations of a climate-tech company at a defining stage, in a small, committed team where your work has direct impact.

·       A key role close to the CEO and the board, with real influence on how Visibuilt is run and scaled.

·       An attractive salary package incl. pension, and participation in our healthcare program.

·       A mission-driven company building bio-based alternatives for construction materials.

·       On-site collaboration in Søborg at Alfa Laval Innovation House.

·       Flexible working hours, so you can plan your work around the rest of your life.

·       Participation in our warrant program and 30 days of paid holiday each year.

Not ticking every box?

Many candidates only apply when they meet every single requirement.

If you recognise yourself in most of this role but not all of it, we would still very much like to hear from you.

Application process

Please apply by 6 November 2026 by emailing your CV (PDF) to job@visibuilt.dk with the subject line “Finance & Operations Manager – [your name]”. We review applications and hold first interviews on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply early. Interviews will take place between 9 and 20 November.

A cover letter is not required. Instead, please answer these five questions briefly in your email:

• 
Are you legally authorized to work in Denmark?

• 
Have you been responsible for month-end close, management reporting and annual accounts, including the auditor process?

• 
Have you reviewed and quality-checked the work of an external accounting partner?

• 
What is your notice period?

• 
What is your level of Danish (none / basic / professional / native)?

We aim to keep the recruitment process fair and unbiased, so please do not include a photo in your CV.

We use AI tools to assist in the initial review of applications; all decisions are made by people.

Today we are 12 people with very different backgrounds, and we would like even more diversity – so whoever you are, we would love to hear from you.

Questions about the position? Please contact Line Kloster Pedersen, CEO, at line@visibuilt.dk, and put job@visibuilt.dk in copy. You are also welcome to call our chairman, Kresten Kloch, on +45 42 82 82 12

Practical note

We would like our new colleague to start on 1 January 2027, or as soon as possible.

We are looking for one or two highly motivated researcher interested in transcription regulation at the DNRF Center of Excellence, Center for Gene Expression (CGEN), within the Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine (ICMM), at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. Starting date: 1st of January 2027 or after agreement.

Information on the department can be found at: https://icmm.ku.dk/english/

Our research

CGEN is an interdisciplinary research center consisting of 6 research groups located in modern laboratories in the Mærsk Tower at the Panum Institute. Our mission is to use a cutting-edge ensemble of genetic, cell biological, biochemical, organismal, and modern ‘omic’-approaches to achieve a comprehensive understanding of the process of gene expression.

CGEN performs ground-breaking research in a collaborative and ambitious environment, where young researchers are offered the best conditions to engage in bold and imaginative research. CGEN is also a center of learning, where PhDs and postdocs receive comprehensive insights in the cellular processes underlying gene expression, as well as a clear view of their medical importance and potential for a future research career.

Information on CGEN and its individual groups can be found at: https://cgen.ku.dk/ and on ICMM at: https://icmm.ku.dk/english/

Your job

The researcher’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

• research, including publication/academic dissemination duties

• research-based teaching and mentorship, primarily in a laboratory setting.

The project will be decided in consultation with the selected candidate(s) in accordance with ongoing research programmes within the individual groups. Broadly projects are focused on understanding the various aspects of the process of gene expression, ranging from the mechanisms of 3D chromatin organisation to transcription, mRNA processing, translation, and protein turnover. CGEN addresses fundamental questions in this broad field at the leading edge of science and aims to dramatically expand our knowledge of the processes, signals and factors allowing a gene to be transcribed while integrating with protein synthesis and protein turnover, so that the overall integrity of gene expression is maintained.

Profile

Six overall criteria apply for researcher appointments at the University of Copenhagen. The six criteria (research, teaching, societal impact, organisational contribution, external funding, and leadership) are considered a framework for the overall assessment of candidates. Find information about each criterion here: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/criteria-for-recognising-merit.

Furthermore, we are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following skills and experience:

Essential experience and skills:

• You have a PhD in life science

• Research qualifications at the level that can be achieved by satisfactorily completing a period of employment as a postdoc but may also be obtained in other ways.

• Research-based teaching or mentorship.

• You are highly experienced in either biochemistry, molecular cell biology, genome-wide analysis, or quantitative imaging in mammalian cells

• You have previous experience within the field of transcription and/or co-transcriptional processing, ideally with a focus on RNAPII regulation

• You possess a high degree of independence, motivation, attention to detail and proactiveness.

• You have excellent time-management, self-organisation and teamwork skills

• We value a problem-solving mindset, strong communication skills, and a collaborative spirit.

Desirable experience and skills:

• Experience with CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing and/or screening approaches

• Experience with techniques to profile nascent transcription, RNAPII occupancy, ribosome footprinting, etc.

• Experience with proteomics to characterise RNAPII elongation complexes

The working language of the department is English and, consequently, the successful applicant must possess excellent skills in written and spoken English. An ability to communicate in Danish is preferable.

Place of employment

The place of employment is at the Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine, Panum, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories located in the Mærsk tower with access to state-of-the-art facilities for cell engineering, next-generation sequencing, flow cytometry, and mass spectrometry.

Scientific environment

The Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine (ICMM) offers an ambitious scientific environment, with many different nationalities represented. ICMM aims to produce research with high international impact focusing on the functional cell, its genetic components and molecular cellular mechanisms in a medical context. ICMM currently comprises five research programmes, three high profile Research Centers as well as a number of international research groups. The scientists at ICMM are involved in high quality research based undergraduate and graduate teaching programs at the University of Copenhagen. You can read more at www.icmm.ku.dk

Terms of employment

The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

The position is a fixed-term position for a period of 6 months, starting on 1st of January 2027. While funding is currently secured for the first 6 months, the possibility of extending the position to one or two years is expected to be clarified during the recruitment process.

Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 40,000 DKK/approx. 5,350 EUR (August 2026-level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.

Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2020.

Questions

For further information please contact Jesper Svejstrup (jsvejstrup@sund.ku.dk), www.sund.ku.dk

Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

Application procedure

Your application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply for position’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

• Motivated letter of application (Max. one page)

• CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position

• A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do

• List of publications

• Teaching portfolio (If applicable)

Deadline for applications: 29 October 2026**, 23.59pm CET**

We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

The further process

After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: 170026 Clinical Professor of Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology (Fixed-Term, 5 Years)
jobs.description:
Clinical Professor of Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology 
 (Fixed-Term, 5 Years)

  Department of Clinical Medicine
 Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences

  University of Copenhagen

  The University seeks to appoint a clinical professor of Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology to commence as soon as possible. The externally funded professorship is combined with a consultancy at Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet, Department of ORL, Head and Neck Surgery and Audiology in the Capital Region.

  It is a requirement for appointment that the applicant is accepted for both the professorship and the consultancy. In order to be considered for the position, the applicant must send two applications: one to the Faculty (the professorship) and one to the hospital (the consultancy) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the consultancy. This also applies to applicants who are already employed as consultants at the Hospital. Please find the advertisement for the consultancy at www.sundhedsjobs.dk/

  Both the professorship and the consultancy will be financed by Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet.

  Find information about the department.

  Job description
 In the consideration of applications for the professorship, the main emphasis will be on the applicant's ability to document a high level of original scientific work at an international level within the area of Otorhinolaryngology.

  The professor's responsibilities will primarily consist of:

   	
• Research, including publication/academic dissemination – The professor is expected to conduct and lead high-quality clinical and translational research within otorhinolaryngology, head and neck surgery and audiology. Relevant research areas that are prioritized will be head and neck surgical oncology and biomarker development. The professor is furthermore expected to contribute to the development and implementation of new diagnostic and treatment approaches within the field. 	
• Research-based teaching, including associated examination – The professor will contribute actively to undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing medical education through research-based teaching. In particular, the professor is expected to contribute to teaching and examination within the Clinical Course in Otorhinolaryngology and the Medical Specialty Focused Course and Exam in Otorhinolaryngology, and to supervise medical students, PhD candidates, and clinical researchers. The professor will contribute to the integration of current research findings into clinical teaching, curriculum development, and specialist training. 	
• Research leadership, including guidance and supervision of researchers – The professor is expected to play a central role in the development and strategic direction of the research environment within otorhinolaryngology, head and neck surgery and audiologThe professor is expected to contribute to innovation and societal impact through the development, evaluation, and implementation of new knowledge, technologies, and clinical practices. 	
• Obligation to share knowledge with the rest of society, including participation in public debate 	
• Academic assessments   Required qualifications 
 To be qualified for a clinical professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution, and leadership. Find information about each criterion.

  Furthermore, each applicant must be able to:

   	
• Document a high degree of original academic production at an international level, including considerable contributions to the development of the academic discipline 	
• Manage research and other management functions, e.g. engage in the university’s external academic activities, as well as knowledge and technology transfer 	
• Provide research-based teaching   The professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.

  Terms of employment 
 The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of five years. Extension is possible if the employed candidate performs well in the position.

  For the professorship the appointee will receive a pensionable annual honorarium of 219.882,33 DKK (1 August 2026 level).

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.

  Questions
 For further information please contact Head of Department Nicolai W. Albrechtsen, nicolai.albrechtsen@regionh.dk.

  Foreign applicants may find the university’s International Staff Mobility useful.

  Application
 The application must be submitted in English and must include the following documents:

   	
• Application (Including motivations for applying for this position (Maximum 2 pages)) 	
• Curriculum vitae (Including information about external funding) 	
• Diplomas (Master’s and PhD and other relevant certificates) 	
• Uploads of maximum 10 publications to be considered in the assessment 	
• Self-declaration form (Template under Nyttige links - Upload the completed and mandatory form as “Other relevant material”) 	
• Teaching portfolio (Guidelines / Template for inspiration under Nyttige links) 	
• Research plan (3‐5 pages) 	
• Teaching plan 	
• A complete list of publications   Application procedure 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee. When the assessment work is completed, each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at the university's Job Portal.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested applicants to apply for this position.

  Please submit the application with the required attachments. Only online applications will be accepted. The closing date for applications is 23.59 p.m. CET, Sunday, 8 November 2026.

  Interviews for this position are likely to be held in the month of March 2027.

jobs.occupation: Associate Professor in Public Health: Children and Young People
jobs.description:
At the National Institute of Public Health (NIPH), University of Southern Denmark (SDU), a position as Associate Professor in Public Health is hereby advertised with a focus on interdisciplinary, qualitative studies of children’s and young people’s health and well-being, commencing on 15 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

About your future research environment  

The National Institute of Public Health (NIPH) is part of the University of Southern Denmark and is located in Copenhagen. As a national public health institute, we conduct research to improve public health in Denmark and Greenland. At the same time, we contribute internationally to the development of knowledge, theories and methods in the field of public health.

We offer an inspiring research environment in the heart of Copenhagen with skilled and dedicated colleagues from diverse research and educational backgrounds. Here, you will have the opportunity for academic exchange and further development of your own research areas, as well as participation in national and international networks. The position is anchored in the research group Health Promotion and Interventions, which conducts research on interventions addressing public health issues and works with methodological and theoretical challenges related to the design and evaluation of intervention and implementation studies. Our research concerns children, young people and families, as well as vulnerable and disadvantaged groups, and takes place in a range of settings, including daycare institutions, primary and lower secondary schools, upper secondary education, the healthcare system, municipal services, supermarkets and local communities.  
You will actively participate in the daily activities of the research group and work closely with other researchers at NIPH.  

The duties include research, teaching and dissemination within the institute’s areas of expertise, including:  
- Children’s and young people’s health, well-being and everyday life
- The significance of digital media for children’s and young people’s lives and health
- Health promotion and implementation research in daycare institutions, schools and upper secondary education
- Interdisciplinary, practice-oriented research and development projects, including process evaluation
- Advanced qualitative methods, including ethnography, interviews, focus groups and child-centred approaches
- Teaching and supervision at bachelor’s and master’s level, including qualitative methods, children’s and young people’s health, and implementation
- Preparation of applications for external funding as well as project management and coordination
- Contributions to the further development of the research environment, including method development and research group activities
 
The following qualifications are highly valued:  
You have established yourself as a qualified researcher within qualitative methods, children’s and young people’s health, and intervention and implementation research, and you possess strong research and teaching qualifications at a high level. You have a relevant publication profile and extensive experience in disseminating research to researchers, practitioners, and other target groups. You have broad collaborative networks and experience in research collaboration with practitioners. As a person, you are dedicated and possess strong communication skills. You are able to build trusting relationships with students, colleagues, and external partners alike. As a teacher, you communicate up-to-date, relevant knowledge in an engaging, clear and understandable way, and as a supervisor you are skilled, inspiring, and supportive.  

Qualifications  
- A PhD degree in Public Health, Education, Sociology, Anthropology or a related field
- Experience with intervention and implementation research
- Documented experience in research on children’s and young people’s health
- A strong profile within qualitative research
- Experience in collaborating with practitioners, exchanging knowledge and disseminating research
- Experience in national and international research collaboration
- Documented teaching experience at university level and experience supervising students (e.g. bachelor’s or master's students)
- Proficiency in Danish and English at a high level, both orally and in writing
- Documented experience with scientific publications within relevant research areas
 

Further information regarding the position can be obtained from:  
Research Leader Susan Andersen,  mailto:suan@sdu.dk

Appointment to the position will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state with the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for associate professor as described herein. Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include:

• 
Motivated application

• 
Curriculum vitae

Master’s degree and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (copy of original + verified English translation)

Teaching portfolio

The Project Manager will be responsible for documentation and one point of contact on all internal centrally driven project activities coming from support functions e.g., engineering, technical support etc. towards sites. • Regional project activities, i.e. WTG planned maintenance and minor corrective activities.

• Project execution and third parties, with special focus on the safe and efficient delivery on offshore operations.

• On site project management, ensuring that centrally driven projects are effectively integrated on site.

• Deliver service packages to site coordinating i.e. planning, spare parts and documentation.

• Manage key interfaces between site and Central Support functions

• Manage and create the site-specific documentation (RAMS etc.)

• Collate and review service reports from contractors/third-parties on site.

• Liaise with contractors/third parties to ensure that the requested skills/training/competences etc. are understood prior to their arrival on site.

Qualifications

• A degree in engineering (marine, electrical, mechanical etc.) or experienced wind turbine technician or other technical education

• Experience within Project Management, Document Creation, Stakeholder Management etc.

• Preferable have relevant work experience e.g. from the wind business, power generation or Operation & Maintenance in a related field

• Strong drive and business mind set

• Good communication, cooperation and organizational skills

• Fluent in Danish and English, written and spoken

We welcome your application in English, including CV and cover letter via the link, no later than the 30th of October 2026.
